_comment: Per-class defaults merged into submission.md. Edit freely. Keys match the --class value on a finding. 'references' is a list. Anything a finding doesn't override falls back to a fill-in stub.

idor.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
idor.impact: An authenticated user can read/modify another user's data by changing an object identifier, with no authorization check enforced server-side. This exposes other users' PII/records and can enable account takeover or data tampering at scale.
idor.remediation: Enforce object-level authorization on the server for every request: verify the authenticated principal owns or may access the referenced object. Do not rely on unguessable IDs; use indirect references or per-user scoping.
references: OWASP API Security Top 10 — API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

xss.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
xss.impact: Attacker-controlled script executes in a victim's browser in the application's origin, enabling session/token theft, actions on the victim's behalf, and credential phishing within the trusted domain.
xss.remediation: Context-aware output encoding on all untrusted data; a strict Content-Security-Policy; framework auto-escaping; HttpOnly on session cookies. For DOM XSS, avoid unsafe sinks (innerHTML, eval) and use safe APIs.

ssrf.impact: The server can be coerced into making requests to attacker-chosen destinations, reaching internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254) — often leading to credential theft and internal network pivoting.
ssrf.remediation: Allowlist outbound destinations; resolve and validate hostnames/IPs (block link-local, private, and metadata ranges) after DNS resolution; disable unneeded URL schemes/redirects; require authentication on internal services.

sqli.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
sqli.impact: Attacker-controlled input alters SQL queries, allowing read/modification of arbitrary database contents, authentication bypass, and in some configurations command execution on the database host.
sqli.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements everywhere; apply least-privilege DB accounts; validate and constrain input; avoid building SQL by string concatenation (including in ORMs' raw fragments).
references: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

ssti.cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
ssti.impact: User input evaluated by a server-side template engine allows template expression injection, commonly escalating to remote code execution on the application server.
ssti.remediation: Never pass user input into template source; use logic-less or sandboxed templates; pass untrusted data only as rendered context variables, not as template text.

rce.cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
rce.impact: Arbitrary command/code execution on the server, giving full control of the application host, its data, and a pivot point into internal infrastructure.
rce.remediation: Eliminate the unsafe sink (shell/exec/deserialization/eval of untrusted input); use safe APIs and allowlists; patch the affected component; run with least privilege and strong egress controls.

csrf.impact: A victim's authenticated session is used to perform state-changing actions they did not intend, from an attacker-controlled page.
csrf.remediation: Anti-CSRF tokens on state-changing requests; SameSite cookies; verify Origin/Referer; require re-authentication for sensitive actions.

auth-bypass.impact: An attacker gains authenticated access, or access to another account, without valid credentials — a direct breach of the authentication boundary.
auth-bypass.remediation: Enforce authentication checks server-side on every protected route; fix the specific bypass (logic flaw, token handling, forced browsing); add tests covering the bypass path.

oauth.impact: Flaws in the OAuth/OIDC flow (redirect_uri handling, state/PKCE, token leakage) enable authorization-code/token theft and account takeover.
oauth.remediation: Strict exact-match redirect_uri allowlisting; enforce state and PKCE; never expose tokens in URLs/Referer; validate token audience and issuer.

ssrf-blind.impact: Blind SSRF confirmed via out-of-band interaction; reachability of internal/attacker-chosen hosts without a direct response channel.
ssrf-blind.remediation: As SSRF: allowlist destinations, validate resolved IPs, block metadata/internal ranges, restrict schemes and redirects.
